{{More citations needed|date=January 2021}}
'''Statistical genetics''' is a scientific field concerned with the development and application of statistical methods for drawing inferences from [[genetics|genetic]] data. The term is most commonly used in the context of [[human genetics]]. Research in statistical genetics generally involves developing theory or methodology to support research in one of three related areas:

*[[population genetics]] - Study of evolutionary processes affecting genetic variation between organisms 
*[[genetic epidemiology]] - Studying effects of genes on diseases<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VC7BAgAAQBAJ&dq=Fundamentals+of+genetic+epidemiology&pg=PP1|title=Fundamentals of Genetic Epidemiology|last1=Khoury|first1=Muin J.|last2=M.D|first2=Director Office of Genetics and Disease Prevention Muin J. Khoury|last3=Beaty|first3=Terri H.|last4=Cohen|first4=Professor of Epidemiology Bernice H.|last5=Cohen|first5=Bernice H.|date=1993|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=9780195052886|language=en}}</ref>
*[[quantitative genetics]] - Studying the effects of genes on 'normal' [[phenotypes]]

Statistical geneticists tend to collaborate closely with [[geneticist]]s, [[molecular biology|molecular biologists]], [[clinical genetics|clinicians]] and [[bioinformatics|bioinformaticians]]. Statistical genetics is a type of [[computational biology]].

==History==
In the early 20th century, R. A. Fisher's 1918 work helped reconcile Mendelian and biometric approaches to continuous traits and introduced the infinitesimal model, which became foundational in quantitative genetics.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Singular effect of linkage on long-term genetic gain in Fisher's infinitesimal model|url=https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/3/8/pgae314/7721206|journal=PNAS Nexus|year=2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Assumption-Free Estimation of Heritability from Genome-Wide Identity-by-Descent Sharing between Full Siblings|url=https://journals.plos.org/plosgenetics/article?id=10.1371/journal.pgen.0020041|journal=PLOS Genetics|year=2006}}</ref>
